questions.question: What happens if an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) breaks down?

options.text: The driver will not notice.
A yellow light will appear on the dashboard.
The brakes will lock up.
The brakes will stop working.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow light will appear on the dashboard.
questions.explanation: When ABS breaks down, a yellow warning light turns on in your dashboard. This light alerts you that there is a problem with the braking system.

questions.question: What should you do when driving?

options.text: Hide what you plan to do from other drivers.
Use turn signals only when other vehicles are nearby.
Do not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn or change lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do. Signal even if no other vehicles are near you.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with air brakes, it activates an electric switch. What does this do?

options.text: Turn off the brake lights.
Turn on the low pressure warning light.
Turn on the brake lights.
Turn off the low pressure warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the brake lights.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure moves an electric switch. This switch turns on the brake lights so other drivers know you are stopping.

questions.question: How can you identify a converter dolly that has ABS?

options.text: By a blue sticker.
By an orange sticker.
By a yellow light on the left side of the dolly.
By a blue light on the left side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: By a yellow light on the left side of the dolly.
questions.explanation: All dollies made after March 1, 1998 must have ABS. You can tell if a dolly has ABS by looking for a yellow light on its left side.

questions.question: What can help reduce stress while driving?

options.text: Drink coffee or other caffeine.
Talk on your cell phone.
Make gestures at other drivers.
Listen to calm music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen to calm music.
questions.explanation: Stress while driving can lead to dangerous behavior. Listening to calm music can help you relax and reduce stress.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving downhill, what is your best option to stop?

options.text: An escape ramp.
Drive onto the shoulder.
Stay on the road.
Hit a slower vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: An escape ramp.
questions.explanation: Use an escape ramp if your brakes fail on a downhill. If no ramp is available, look for another safe route like a side road or open field.

questions.question: What do many drivers do in bad weather?

options.text: Drive in front of trucks.
Drive beside trucks.
Follow closely behind trucks.
Drive without lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow closely behind trucks.
questions.explanation: In bad weather when it is hard to see, many drivers follow trucks closely. Keep a safe distance from the vehicle in front of you if someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: What equipment must truck tractors with air brakes have if they were built after March 1, 1997?

options.text: An extra set of brakes.
Voice-activated brakes.
Cruise control.
Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.correctAnswerText: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes made after March 1, 1997 must have ABS. Other vehicles with air brakes made after March 1, 1998 must also have ABS.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a cause of vehicle fires?

options.text: Tires that are not filled with enough air.
Problems in the electrical system.
Flammable cargo.
Rolling down the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rolling down the window.
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires can be caused by low tire pressure, damaged electrical systems, spilled fuel, loose fuel connections, smoking near fuel, and improper flammable cargo. Rolling down a window cannot cause a fire.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning light?

options.text: Turn the parking brake on and off.
Push and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
Open the rear shut-off valves.
Disconnect and reconnect all connections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: To test the warning light, let the air system fill up first. Then push and release the brake pedal quickly several times. This releases air and the warning light should turn on when air pressure gets too low.

questions.question: Why should flares be used carefully after an accident?

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares.
Flares are expensive.
Other drivers may become confused about what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Spilled fuel and improper use of flares can cause a fire after an accident.

questions.question: What happens if an engine runs without oil?

options.text: The vehicle will run smoothly.
The vehicle will make jerky movements while driving.
The engine can be damaged quickly.
Gas mileage will improve.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be damaged quickly.
questions.explanation: An engine can be destroyed rapidly without oil. If your oil pressure gauge shows low or changing pressure, do not drive the vehicle.

questions.question: Can radial and bias-ply tires be used together?

options.text: Yes, they can be used together on all axles.
Yes, but only on the rear axle.
No, they should not be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they should not be used together.
questions.explanation: When checking your vehicle, make sure you are not using radial and bias-ply tires together.

questions.question: What is the best way to check your lights during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Park near a mirror to see the reflection.
Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
Check if any warning lights show up on the dashboard.
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to signal if lights are out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and then exit the vehicle to check them.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A warning system.
A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks.
A noise made by air brakes when used.
A part in the braking unit that lets air move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning system.
questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device in an air brake system. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi.

questions.question: How can you best tell if your trailer is starting to skid?

options.text: By looking at other drivers' faces.
By seeing it in your mirrors.
By feeling it.
By listening to the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: By seeing it in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: The earliest and best way to detect a trailer skid is by seeing the trailer move off-course in your mirrors.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning usually occur?

options.text: When tires are properly inflated.
At speeds under 15 mph.
In areas where water sits on the road.
During the evening.

questions.correctAnswerText: In areas where water sits on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen where water collects on the road. Low tire pressure and worn tread make it more likely. If there is enough water on the road, hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Trust the posted signals to tell you when a train is coming.
Watch other drivers to see if a train is coming.
Do not rely only on signals to tell you when a train is coming.
Look at nearby plants to see if they move from the wind of a passing train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on signals to tell you when a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Always approach a railroad crossing assuming a train might be coming. Do not depend only on signals or hearing to know if a train is near.

questions.question: When driving down a steep grade, your brakes may fade. What does brake fade mean?

options.text: They become quieter.
They become less effective.
They work better than usual.
They work differently from front to back.

questions.correctAnswerText: They become less effective.
questions.explanation: Using brakes too much on a steep downgrade can cause them to overheat and work less effectively. To avoid overheating your brakes on a steep hill, use engine braking.

questions.question: When parking a double or triple trailer, what kind of parking space should you look for?

options.text: A space that is easy to enter and exit.
A space close to parked cars.
A space on the grass, away from other vehicles.
A space directly in front of a building.

questions.correctAnswerText: A space that is easy to enter and exit.
questions.explanation: Because you cannot see everything behind you, backing is always dangerous and should be avoided. Choose parking spaces where you can pull forward when you leave.
